patch.value:
## Observed

`pm close <id> "<reason>"` without `--completed-at` sets `completed_at` to the close time, and nothing records that the value was defaulted rather than asserted. Agents that close work retroactively (tracker reconciliation, a sweep after PRs merged, closing a delivered item the next session) almost never pass `--completed-at`, so the tracker silently records delivery at reconciliation time.

Measured on 2026-10-24/25 in a 31-repository fleet: a reconciliation sweep closed 109 delivered items, every one with `completed_at` = sweep time although each close reason cited a PR merged 1–20 days earlier. Consumers that read `completed_at` as the delivery time (cycle time, burndown, Gantt bars, a memory package's recall-utility scoring) were all wrong until each item was corrected with `pm update <id> --completed-at <merge time>`. A review bot caught it on one repository; the other 30 had passed review.

## Expected

The defaulted value should be distinguishable from an asserted one, and the CLI should nudge at the moment the mistake happens. For example:

1. **Provenance:** record `completed_at_source: "close_time" | "asserted"` (or an equivalent history-event flag), so consumers can exclude or flag defaulted completion times.
2. **Hint on retroactive closes:** when `pm close` runs without `--completed-at` and the item shows no substantive activity for N hours (or the close reason contains an ISO timestamp earlier than now), return a `hints[]` entry: `completed_at defaults to the close time; pass --completed-at <ISO> if the work finished earlier` with the exact command.
3. Optionally `pm close --completed-at from-reason` to take the earliest ISO timestamp in the close reason.

## Why it matters for agents

Agents close items in batches long after delivery much more often than humans do, and `completed_at` is the field every analytics consumer trusts. A silent default turns one forgotten flag into wrong data in every downstream report, with no way to tell after the fact.

Version: `@unbrained/pm-cli` 2026.10.24.
